correctness.rationale: For the exact ordinary-cut Alexander dual every vertex triple must be connected. For triangle-free periodic grids, the only tetrahedra are unit four-cycles, and every triangle is an induced 2-path. The proof supplies an explicit uniform sequence of N tetrahedron-triangle collapses, N square-diagonal/triangle collapses, and 2N straight-chord/triangle collapses, all with free faces by unique-square and unique-common-neighbor properties. The remaining complex is the standard triangulated torus plus N(N-13)/2 extra edges, hence T^2 wedge L circles, giving integral cohomology Z^(L+2) in degree one and Z in degree two. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality yields Z in ordinary cut degree N-5 and Z^(L+2) in degree N-4, and no other reduced groups. The actual standalone verify.py passed full local free-face checks and residual face equality on (5,5),(5,6),(6,6),(5,7), plus exhaustive five-subset tests on the first two. The infinite theorem is proved structurally; finite runs are corroboration. Limits below m,n=5 excluded.

originality.rationale: The inspected arXiv foundational papers and the four close full-text publicly indexed results do not cover the ordinary three-cut complex of periodic products of two cycles with the stated two-degree integral homology. Edge-disjoint-square assumptions fail; path grids have nonperiodic disk boundaries; the Čech and total-two-cut criteria differ; I_3 forbids only independent triples, not all disconnected triples. Targeted published-finding corpus query variants and accessible historical own-claim overlaps gave no exact or implied equivalent. Bibliographic novelty remains qualified by unindexed or inaccessible work.

value.rationale: A complete torsion-free integral homology formula for the natural, infinite two-parameter family C_m square C_n with m,n≥5, plus an integral homotopy decomposition of its combinatorial Alexander dual. The difference between disk-filling rectangular grids and periodic torus filling creates an essential genus-one fundamental class in a degree strictly below the pure cut-complex top degree, uniformly proving nonshellability. The nonzero cup product and the geometrically motivated circle count go beyond a small rank computation or a trivial specialization.
